From sea to great sea he will rule by his worth,
The river Euphrates to ends of the earth.

The tribes of the desert will bow before him;
His enemies, too, will lick dust before him.
The great kings of Tarshish and of distant shores
will bring to him tribute of great precious ores.

The kings of both Sheba and Seba are there,
Presenting him gifts of their kingdoms most fair.
All kings of the earth will bow down to his fame;
All nations will serve him and honor his name.

For he will deliver the needy who cry;
He’ll help the afflicted when no one is nigh.
He will take great pity on both poor and weak;
The needy near death, he will save and will seek.

He’ll rescue them from great oppression and might,
For their blood is precious and dear in his sight.
O long may he live! Sheba’s gold pave his way;
Let people pray for him and bless him all day.

Let grain in abundance abound through the land,
On tops of the hills sway, and fruitfully stand;
Its fruit be like Lebanon’s bountiful yield,
To flourish and thrive like the grass of the field.

May his name forever endure like the sun;
All nations be bless’d through him—and bless that one.
Now bless’d be the Lord, praise to Him let us bring—
To the God of Isr’el who does wondrous things.

Praise be to His glo-ri-ous name for all days;
May all earth be filled with His glory and praise.
The Lord God of Is-ra-el, praise without end,
The whole earth will praise Him—Amen and Amen!

title: Psalm 73
lyrics:
Surely God is good to Isr’el, to those who are pure in heart.
As for me, my feet slipped and my foothold nearly fell apart.
For the arrogant I envied, when they had prosperity;
For they seem to have no struggles, strong in health they seem to be.

They are free from common burdens—human ills our lives have borne.
Therefore pride is like their necklace; vi-o-lence like clothing worn.
From their callous hearts come evil; plots within their minds do grow.
And they scoff, they speak with malice, and oppressive threats they show.

They have set their mouths ’gainst heaven, and their tongues parade the earth.
Therefore, people turn to them and drink up words that have no worth.
They say, “How can God know of us? Can the Most High knowledge teach?”
This is what the wicked look like—carefree and in wealth increased.

Surely it’s in vain I’ve kept my heart and conscience right and pure;
In vain have I washed my hands in innocence, kept my steps sure.
All day long I have been stricken, chastened every morning new.
If I had said, “I will speak thus”—I’d betray Your children true.

When I tried to understand this, it was heavy in my sight,
Till I saw God’s sanctuary, entered and saw their true plight.
Surely they are set by God on slipp’ry ground; to ruin cast—
Suddenly, they are destroyed and swept away by terror fast.

Like a dream when one awakens, so when You arise, O Lord;
You will then despise their image—they who gave You no accord.
When my heart was grieved, embittered, I was like a beast to You;
I was ignorant and senseless; could not see Your way so true.

Yet, O Lord, I’m always with You; You hold me by my right hand.
With your counsel, You will guide me, and make me in glory stand.
Whom have I in heav’n but You, Lord? And on earth want nothing more.
Though my heart and flesh may fail me, God’s my portion evermore.

All of those who are far from You, they will perish, one and all;
You destroy all the unfaithful, who upon You do not call.
As for me, it is so good that God is near in all my needs;
I have made the Lord my refuge, and will tell of all Your deeds.

title: Psalm 74
lyrics:
Why have You long rejected us, O God?
Why does Your anger burn against Your sheep?
You purchased us—Your own inheritance;
Remember those You saved; Mount Zion keep.

Turn Your steps toward this devastation great;
The enemy destroyed the holy place.
Your foes have roared into Your meeting place,
They’ve set up standards as signs of disgrace.

They’ve taken axes as men would chop trees;
They’ve smashed the carved work, brought unholy shame.
They burned Your sanctuary to the ground;
Defiled the dwelling place of Your great name.

They said within their hearts, “We’ll crush them whole!”
They burned each place where worship was of Thee.
No mighty signs or prophets can be found,
And none of us knows how long this will be.

How long, O God, will foes deride Your name?
How long will enemies their scorn deploy?
Why do You hold Your hand back and delay?
Take Your right hand from waiting, and destroy!

But You, O God, are my king from of old;
You bring salvation unto all the earth.
You split the seas wide open by Your pow’r;
You crushed the monsters and Levi’than’s girth.

You opened springs and dried up rivers’ flow;
The day and night, sun, moon belong to You.
You set earth’s bound’ries—where they end, You know;
You made the summer and the winter, too.

Now, Lord, remember how Your foes have mocked;
How foolish people have reviled Your name.
Don’t hand Your dove to wild beasts to devour,
And don’t forget Your people, clothed in shame.

Keep Your own cov-e-nant, O Lord, in mind,
For vio-lence fills dark places in the land.
Don’t let the oppressed ones tremble in disgrace,
But may the needy praise Your name and stand.

Rise up, O God, and now defend Your cause;
See how fools mock You all day scornfully.
Do not ignore the clamor of Your foes;
Their uproar rises up continually.

title: Psalm 75
lyrics:
We give thanks to You, O God,
Your name’s near—give thanks abroad.
All tell of Your wondrous deeds,
We give thanks, Your name we heed.
You say, “I appoint the time;
Judge uprightly all that’s Mine.

“When the earth and peoples quake,
I won’t let earth’s pillars shake.Selah
To the proud I say, ‘Boast not!’
To the wicked, ‘Horns are naught!’
Don’t lift up your horns on high,
Don’t speak with your head held high.”

No one from the east or west
can exalt a man at best.
God it is who judges all;
He exalts or makes us fall.
The Lord’s hand holds forth a cup
full of wine with spice mixed up.

Foaming wine He will pour out;
All earth’s wicked cry and shout.
To the dregs they drink it down.
As for me, with a great sound,
I’ll declare and sing God’s praise—
God of Jacob, all my days.

He will find the horns of those
wicked ones who Him oppose;
All their horns will be cut off,
Those who at Him sneer and scoff.
But the horns of righteous men
will be lifted up again.

title: Psalm 76
lyrics:
In Judah God is known; His name in Is-ra-el.
His tent is in Jerusalem—in Zion He does dwell.
For there He broke the spears, the flashing arrows bright,
The swords and shields, the weapons of all war by His great might.Selah

Your glo-rious light shines forth, majestic more than hills,
Or mountains that are rich with game—with glo-rious light You’re filled.
The brave and valiant men lie plundered, cannot stand;
They sleep their last—no warrior’s left who can lift up his hand.

At Your rebuke, O God; O God of Jacob still;
At Your rebuke, both horse and man with char-i-ot lie still.
You’re to be feared alone; before You who can stand?
When You are angry, who can stand before Your righteous hand?

From heav-en judgment came; the earth was still with fear—
When You, O God, rose up to judge, to save afflicted here.Selah
For e’en the wrath of man will be turned to Your praise;
And with the wrath that does remain, You’ll gird Yourself like praise.

Make vows unto the Lord, fulfill them and draw near.
Let all the lands around bring gifts to Him who’s to be feared.
He breaks the pride of those who do not see His worth,
Then He is feared by rulers great, by kings of all the earth.

title: Psalm 77
lyrics:
I cried out to my God for help; I cried for God to hear.
When in distress, I sought the Lord; no comfort was found near.

All night I stretched untiring hands; my soul could only moan.
I mused, my spirit grew more faint; remembered God and groaned.Selah

You kept my eyes from closing, Lord; too troubled e’en to speak.
I thought of days from long ago, when faith did not seem weak.

My songs remembered in the night bring mem’ry to my heart.
My spirit does inquire of God; with musing, questions start:

“Will God reject forever? O where has His favor gone?
Has His unfailing love now failed? His promise trusted long?

“Has God forgotten to be kind and merciful to me?
Has He in anger withheld love? No mercy do I see!”Selah

And then I thought, “It is my grief to fear and wonder why;
I will appeal to God’s right hand—the years of the Most High.”

I will remember the Lord’s deeds, Your miracles of old.
I’ll meditate on all Your works, Your mighty deeds once told.

Your ways, O God, are holy—for what god’s great as our God?
O God, You do great miracles, display Your pow’r abroad.

Your mighty arm redeemed the host of people who descend
from Jacob and from Joseph—You great help to them did send.Selah

The waters saw You and they shook; the waters saw with fear.
The very depths were shaken when Your presence, God, drew near.

The clouds outpoured their water, and the skies with thunder shook;
Your lightning arrows flashed about—all trembled at Your look.

Your thunder in the whirlwind roared, and all who heard did shake;
Your lightning lit the world, and all the earth did fear and quake.

Your path led through the mighty sea; Your way through waters deep.
And though Your footprints were not seen, Your people You did keep.

You led Your people like a flock that trusts the shepherd’s hand;
Through Moses and through Aaron, You enabled them to stand.

title: Psalm 78
lyrics:
Come listen, O my people, to the teaching we’ve been told.
My mouth will speak in parables, things hidden from of old.
What we have heard and we have known, our fathers told each one,
We’ll not hide from our children, but will tell what God has done.

We’ll tell the praises of the Lord, His pow’r and wonders wrought,
The statutes giv’n to Jacob and the law which we were taught;
So that each generation and the children yet unborn,
Would know these things and in their turn, would tell of God the Lord.

Our children, then, would trust in God, and not forget His deeds;
But they would keep all His commands; His covenant they’d heed.
They’d not be like our fathers were, who stumbled and rebelled—
Those stubborn ones, unfaithful to the God of Israel.

For Ephra’m’s men, though armed with bows, yet turned back from the fray;
Refused to keep God’s covenant; His law would not obey.
Forgetting all that He had done, the wonders by His hand,
The miracles done in their sight, in Egypt’s land, Zo-an.

He led them through divided sea; made water stand upright.
He guided them with cloud by day, with light from fire all night.
He split the rocks in desert land, gave water great as seas.
He brought them streams out of the rock that flowed abundantly.

But they continued in their sin; rebelled ’gainst the Most High;
They put God to the test when they demanded food and cried.
They spoke against Him as they said, “Can God produce this feat?
He struck the rock for water, but can He supply us meat?”

The Lord heard them—His anger burned, His fire on Isr’el came;
For they did not believe in God or trust that He could save.
Yet still He gave command to heav’n, to open wide the door;
He rained down manna for their food, gave bread of heav’n and more.

Men ate the bread of angels—God sent them all they could eat.
He loosed the winds from heaven, and sent birds to them for meat.
He made them come inside their camp, in tents their hands had made.
They ate till they had no more lack; He gave them what they craved.

But while they still were eating food—it still was in their mouths,
God’s anger rose against them and their men He did strike down.
In spite of this, they sinned the more—they turned defiantly;
So He ended their years in fear and in futility.

When God slew them, they turned to Him, to seek Him once again;
For God Most High, their Rock and their Redeemer e’er had been.
But then their mouths would flatter Him, and with their tongues they’d lie;
Their hearts were still unfaithful to His cov’nant from on high.

Yet in His mercy, He forgave; did not destroy their path;
Time after time, held anger back; did not stir up His wrath.
For He remembered they were flesh, a breeze that does not stand.
How often they rebelled ’gainst Him in that great desert land!

The Holy One of Is-ra-el they grieved repeatedly,
For they forgot His pow’r the day He saved and set them free:
How He displayed His wondrous signs in Egypt and Zo-an;
He turned their rivers into blood, no wholesome water ran.

He sent them swarms of flies, and frogs that devastated them.
To grasshoppers, He gave their crops—the locusts finished them.
With hail and sleet destroyed their vines; their cattle also fell.
His anger, wrath, destruction He unleashed through His an-gels.

He spared them not from death and plague; His anger found a path—
He struck down Egypt’s firstborn sons, Ham’s first-fruits knew His wrath.
But He brought forth His people like a flock of sheep safely;
He guided them, but the great sea engulfed their enemy.

Thus He brought them up to the edge of His new holy land.
He drove out nations, so the tribes of Isr’el there could stand.
They put God to the test again, though He had heard their cry.
They did not keep His law, and they rebelled ’gainst the Most High.

Just like their fathers, they rebelled in their unfaithfulness;
They angered Him with idols and false gods they did confess.
When God heard them, His anger burned, His jealousy arose;
He turned from Isr’el and the tent at Shiloh that He chose.

He sent the ark of His great might into captivity—
His splendor and His light into the hands of enemies.
He gave His people to the sword; His fire consumed their men;
Their priests were killed, their widows and their maids were grieving then.

Then God awoke as from a sleep, as man wakes from much wine;
He beat back all His enemies; and shamed them in His time.
The tents of Joseph He chose not, nor tribe of Eph-ra-im;
But Judah’s tribe and Zion’s Mount, He loved and He chose them.

He built His sanctuary like the heights of earth built sure,
And He chose David there to be His servant evermore.
From tending sheep was David brought to shepherd Israel,
And with integrity of heart and skill he led them well.

title: Psalm 79
lyrics:
The nations have invaded Your heritage, O God;
They have defiled Your temple; Jerus’lem’s razed to sod.
They’ve given the dead bodies of Your own saints for meat,
As food for birds of hea-ven, and beasts of earth to eat.

Their blood’s poured out like water around Jerusalem,
And no one’s left alive there to care or bury them.
We’re objects of reproach to our neighbors everywhere,
Of scorn and of derision to everyone who’s there.

How long, O Lord? Forever will You be filled with ire?
How long will You be jealous—Your anger burn like fire?
Pour out Your wrath on nations who do not know Your fame;
Your anger upon kingdoms that don’t call on Your name.

For they’ve devoured Jacob, his homeland laid to waste.
Don’t hold past sins against us; we need You—come in haste!
O help us, God our Savior! For glory of Your name,
Deliver and forgive us, for the sake of Your name.

Why should the nations, boasting, in pride say, “Where’s their God?”
Before our eyes, make known to the nations far abroad,
That You avenge Your people and see their blood outpoured;
That You, before our eyes, show Yourself to be the Lord.

May groaning of the pris’ners come to Your ear and eye;
By strength of Your own arm, Lord, preserve those doomed to die.
Pay back into the laps of our neighbors sevenfold
the scorn they’ve hurled at You, Lord, reproaches brash and bold.

Then we who are Your people—the sheep of Your own field
will thank You, Lord, forever; all praise to You we’ll yield.
And from one generation unto all length of days,
We will recount Your glory, and will tell forth Your praise.

title: Psalm 80
lyrics:
Hear us, O King of Is-ra-el, who shepherds Joseph very well;
And like a flock You care for him, enthroned between the cherubim.
Shine forth before Your people in Manasseh, Ephra’m, Benjamin;
Awaken in Your righteous might, and come to save us in Your light.

Restore us, God, and make Your face to shine upon us by Your grace.
Restore us, God, that we may be forever saved eternally.

O Lord, the God of Hosts, how long will You be angry and prolong
Your wrath against Your people’s prayers, whom You have fed with bread of tears?
For You have made us drink our tears and with our neighbors strive with fears.
Now all our enemies around mock us with scorn, our lives confound.

Restore us, God, and make Your face to shine upon us by Your grace.
Restore, Almighty God, that we may now be saved eternally.

You brought Your people like a vine from Egypt by Your own design;
You drove out all the nations so the vine You planted there could grow.
You cleared the ground and it took root; it filled the land—a sturdy shoot;
The mountains and the cedars tall were covered with its shade o’er all.

Its branches reached to the Great Sea, and to the River Eu-phra-tes.
So why have You now broken down the walls which You once built around?
Now all who pass by pick its fruit, and beasts now ravage and uproot.
Return, O God, look down and see; watch o’er Your vine—Your son indeed!

Your vine is cut and burned with fire; at Your rebuke we all expire.
Let Your hand rest upon the man, the son of man at Your right hand.
Then we will never turn away, from You who are our strength and stay;
Revive us, Lord and we will call upon Your name to save us all.

Restore us, God, and make Your face to shine upon us by Your grace.
O Lord, Almighty God, restore; may we be saved forevermore.

title: Psalm 81
Psalm 82
Psalm 83
lyrics:
O my God, do not keep silent; be not quiet, be not still!
For Your foes make such an uproar, rear their heads against Your will.
They make plans against Your people; plot against those You adore.
They say, “Come, let us destroy them; Isr’el’s name will be no more.”

With one mind they plot together; form alliance against You;
Tents of Edom and of Ishm’el; Moab and the Hagrites, too.
Gebal, Amalek, and Ammon; those of Tyre, Philistia, then—
E’en Assyria has joined them to lend strength to Lot’s children.Selah

Do to them as You fought Mi-dian; let them find what Jabin found,
Who, with Sis-er-a at Kishon, died as dung on Endor’s ground.
Make their nobles be like Oreb, and like Zeeb their leaders be;
All their princes be like Zebah, and Zalmunna ruined be.

All these said, “Let’s take possession, all God’s pastureland we’ll win.”
Like the tumbleweed now make them; like the chaff before the wind.
As the fire consumes the forest, or a flame sets hills on fire,
So pursue them with Your tempest; terrify with Your storm’s ire.

Fill their faces with dishonor, so that they will seek Your Name.
Lord, make them dismayed, and may they perish in disgrace and shame.
Let them know that You alone, Lord—You whose name is full of worth—
You alone are the Most High for You rule over all the earth.

title: Psalm 84
lyrics:
How lovely is Your dwelling place, Almighty God and Lord!
For my soul yearns and even faints to be within Your courts!
My heart and flesh cry out in me, for God, the living God—
Your presence is where I would be; I long for You, my God!

The sparrow even found a home, the swallow found a nest,
Where she may have her young near You, and at Your altar rest.
O Lord Almighty, King and God, how bless-ed are those who
dwell in Your house where they may be forever praising You. Selah

How bless’d are those who find their strength in You, their God and King;
Who set their hearts on pilgrimage, and in Your presence sing.
Through valleys filled with tears they pass, make it a place of springs,
The autumn rains do cover it with pools which the rain brings.

They go from strength to strength until before God they appear;
O listen, God of Jacob and O Lord Almighty, hear!Selah
Now look upon our shield, O God, on Your anointed one;
O look with favor on the face of Your anointed one.

Much better is a day within Your courts where You abide
than thousands where the wicked dwell, who are not on Your side.
For I would rather be a slave, a keeper of the door,
Than live with those in wicked tents who do the Lord ignore.

The Lord is both a sun and shield, and favor He bestows,
And no good thing does He withhold from those whose way He knows—
From those who walk in righteousness, in upright ways and true.
O Lord Almighty, bless’d are those who put their trust in You.

title: Psalm 85
lyrics:
Lord, You showed Your land Your favor
and restored us bountif’lly.
All our sin with grace You covered
and forgave iniquity.Selah

You withdrew Your burning anger,
Turned away from Your fierce wrath.
Now, once more, O God our Savior,
Restore us who seek Your path.

Will Your anger last forever?
To all ages wrath prolong?
Will You not again revive us
that we may rejoice in song?

Show us now Your lovingkindness,
Grant us Your salvation, Lord.
I will listen to what God says:
Peace to those who Him adore.

Let them not return to folly
for salvation is quite near;
In our land may the Lord’s glory
dwell with those who do God fear.

Love and truth have met together,
Righteousness and peace kiss; then
faithfulness springs forth from earth and
righteousness looks down from heav’n.

For the Lord will give what’s good and
then our land its fruit will yield;
Righteousness will go before Him,
Make His steps a path revealed.

title: Psalm 86
Psalm 87
lyrics:
He has set His own foundation on the holy mount of God.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than Jacob’s vast abodes.
Glorious things of you are spoken, Zion, city of our God! Selah
“I will mention all who know Me, who acknowledge me as God:

“I name Babylon and Rahab, Tyre and Cush, Philistia, too;
I will say of them, ‘In Zion, these were born—not just a few!’”
For of Zion it is said that, “This one, that one, here were born,
And the Lord Most High Himself will her establish like the morn.

Then the Lord will write within the registry of peoples all:
“This one here was born in Zion where God’s people on Him call.”Selah
Then all those who do make music, they will sing with joyful tune,
“All the springs of joy abundant; all my fountains are in You!”

title: Psalm 88
lyrics:
O Lord God, the God who saves me; day and night I cry to You.
Turn Your ear to hear my anguish; may my prayer come before You.
For my soul is full of trouble, and my life draws near the grave;
I’m like those who lose all strength and sink to pits where none can save.

I am counted with the dying, like the dead already there;
Not remembered, even by You; fully cut off from Your care.
You have put me in the depths and in the lowest pit I’m cast;
Your wrath lies like weight upon me; with Your waves, I’m drowned at last.Selah

You have taken close friends from me, made me be abhorred by them.
I am trapped, cannot escape and with much grief my eyes are dim.
Yet I daily call to You, Lord; I spread out my hands to You.
Will You show the dead Your wonders? Will the dead rise and praise You? Selah

Is Your love declared in death and is Your faithfulness there found?
Are Your wonders known in darkness? Can Your righteousness abound?
Still I cry to You for help, Lord; in the morning my prayers rise.
Why, O Lord, do You reject me, hide Your face from my worn eyes?

From my youth, I’ve been afflicted, close to death and in despair,
And Your wrath has swept around me, terrors kept me from Your care.
All day long those fears surround me, and engulf me without end.
You take friends and loved ones from me; darkness is my closest friend.

title: Psalm 89
lyrics:
I’ll sing the Lord’s love forever, with my mouth I’ll make Him known;
Faithfulness which leaves us never; His love is upon the throne!
You said, “I have made a cov’nant with the chosen of My hand—
David is My chosen servant; his throne will forever stand.” Selah

Heav’n declares Your wonders, Lord; Your faithfulness ’midst holy ones;
Who is like the Lord in skies above or midst the heav’nly ones?
In the council of the holy, God is greatly to be feared.
Lord Almighty, who is like You? You are faithful and revered!

You rule o’er the surging ocean; You still all the raging sea.
You crushed Egypt with one motion; Your strong arm made Your foes flee.
Heav’n is Yours and earth below it, north and south are in Your sight,
Tabor, Hermon join in worship; Your right hand is full of might.

Your throne rests upon true justice; love and faithfulness are Yours.
Bless’d are those who do acclaim You, and walk in Your light, O Lord.
All day long they praise Your glory, find joy in Your holy name.
Your great strength is all their story—Holy One of Isr’el’s fame!

Once You spoke to us, Your people: “I’ve exalted one from them;
I’ve called David as My servant, and with oil anointed him.
My hand and arm will sustain him; no foes will oppression bring;
I will strike his adversaries; crushing those against My king.

“Faithful love will rest upon him; through My name his horn is high.
His hand will be o’er the seas, and ‘Father, God, my Rock,’ he’ll cry!
I will name him as My firstborn, most exalted of all kings;
I’ll maintain my love forever, and my cov’nant o’er all things.

“I’ll establish him forever through his line and through his throne;
His throne will endure forever, like the heavens he’ll be known.
If his sons forsake My statutes, and don’t follow My decrees,
I’ll repay their sin with flogging, but from him My love won’t flee.

“I won’t violate my cov’nant; never change what I have said;
I have sworn and won’t relent, for David’s line will ever spread!
His throne will endure forever like the sun that shines on high;
It will be established ever, like the moon’s light in the sky!”Selah

But You’re angry with Your servant; You have spurned him, broke Your trust;
You’ve renounced Your faithful cov’nant; thrown his crown into the dust.
You have broken through his stronghold, all who pass have plundered him.
He’s become the scorn of neighbors; You’ve made foes rejoice o’er him.

His drawn sword has now been turned back; You forsook him in the fight.
His bright splendor has all turned black; his throne cast down from his sight!
You’ve cut short the days of his youth, covered him with cloak of shame.Selah
How long, Lord? How long will You hide and Your wrath burn like a flame?

Lord, remember just how fleeting is the measure of my life;
Only for futility have You made men with endless strife.
Who can live and not see death? Or who can from grave’s power flee? Selah
Lord, where is your former love you swore to David faithfully?

Lord, remember how Your servant has been mocked most scornfully;
How I bear within my heart the taunts of nations endlessly.
Taunts, O Lord, which enemies have heaped upon Your chosen one.
Blessed be the Lord forever! Yes, Amen and yes, Amen!

title: Psalm 90
lyrics:
Lord, You have been our dwelling place, through generations all;
From age to age, our hiding place; our refuge whom we call.

Before the mountains came to be, or earth sprang from Your word,
From everlasting to all time, You are the only God.

You turn us back to dust and say, “Return, O sons of men.”
For dust we are, to dust return; we go to dust again.

A thousand years are merely like a day within Your sight;
A day soon gone, or like a watch that passes in the night.

We’re swept away in sleep of death, and like new grass at morn—
Though it sprouts up with morning light, by dusk it’s dry and worn.

For by Your anger we’re consumed—in terror at Your wrath;
You’ve set our sins before You, and Your light reveals their path.

Our days pass quickly in Your wrath; years like a sigh are past.
Our length of days is seventy, or eighty if strength last.

And yet their span is trouble-filled, and sorrow marks our way;
Days quickly pass and soon are gone, and we just fly away.

Who knows the pow-er of Your wrath? It’s great as fear You’re due!
Teach us to number right our days, and gain Your wisdom true.

Relent, O Lord! How long till You have mercy on Your saints?
Come satisfy us in the morn with love that never faints.

Then we will sing for joy, and will be glad for all our days.
O make us glad as many days as we’ve known troubled ways.

May Your deeds and Your works be shown unto Your servants all;
Your splendor to their children and to those who on You call.

May God’s good favor rest on us—our work before Him stand.
Yes, Lord our God, establish firm the work of our own hands.

title: Psalm 91
lyrics:
Those who dwell within the shelter of the Most High who is God;
They’ll abide within the shadow of the true Almighty God.
I will say of Him, the Lord, “He is my refuge, whom I trust;
He’s my God, my strength and fortress, in Him I will put my trust.”

Surely He will save you from the fowler’s snare and pestilence;
With His feathers He will cover, and will be your sure defense.
You will find your constant refuge in the shadow of His wings,
And His faithfulness will be your shield and rampart in all things.

You won’t fear the night’s dark terror, nor the arrow in the day,
Nor the pestilence of darkness, nor the plague’s destructive way.
Though a thousand at your side fall, or ten thousand at your hand,
You won’t be harmed; you’ll just see how all the wicked do not stand.

The Most High—if He’s your dwelling—if the Lord’s your confidence,
Then no harm will come upon you, nor disaster near your tents.
For His angels will surround you, guard you in your ways alone.
They will lift you in their hands so that your foot won’t strike a stone.

You will tread upon the lion, and the cobra without fear;
You will trample the great lion, and the serpent who comes near.
The Lord says, “Because he loves Me, I will rescue him from shame;
I’ll protect him from all danger—he acknowledges My name.

“He will call to Me—I’ll answer; when he cries out, I will hear.
I’ll deliver him with honor; in his trouble I’ll be near.
With long life, I’ll satisfy him, till the time his days will cease;
I will show him My salvation—he will dwell within My peace.”

title: Psalm 92
lyrics:
It’s good to praise the Lord and make music to Your name,
O Most High, in the morning Your love we will proclaim.
We’ll sing Your faithfulness in the night—the lyre we’ll play,
With songs upon the harp we will praise You all the day.

For You have made me glad by Your deeds, O sovereign Lord;
I sing for joy at all of the works Your hands put forth.
How great Your works, O Lord, how profound and vast Your thoughts!
The senseless and the fools do not fathom as they ought!

They do not understand that like grass the wicked grow—
They may spring up and flourish, the ones who evil know.
But they will be destroyed, and no longer will remain,
Yet You, O Lord, forever exalted always reign.

For surely all Your foes, Lord, will perish thoroughly;
Your enemies be scattered, all evildoers flee.
But You have lifted high and exalted my horn’s strength,
And poured fine oil upon me, with honor of great length.

My eyes have seen the final defeat of all my foes;
My ears have heard the routing of them who me oppose.
The righteous ones will flourish like palm trees ever green;
They’ll grow like Leb’non’s cedars with grandeur ever seen.

They’ll be a fertile planting in the house of the Lord.
They’ll flourish in God’s courts and stay green as age endures.
They’ll bear fruit in old age, and proclaim, “The Lord’s upright!
He is my rock and there is no evil in His sight!”

title: Psalm 93
lyrics:
The Lord reigns, and He is robed in majesty and strength divine;
He has armed Himself with strength and does with splendor fully shine.
The world is established firmly; it cannot be ever moved.
Your throne is established ever; from all ages You are God!

Seas have lifted up, O Lord, the seas have lifted up their voice;
Seas lift up their pounding waves, but greater than their thund’rous noise—
Might-ier than the seas’ great breakers, God the Lord on high is more.
Holiness adorns Your house, Lord; Your laws stand forever sure.

title: Psalm 94
lyrics:
O Lord God, the God of vengeance, who avenges, now shine forth.
Rise up, Judge of all the earth, from east and west, from south and north.
Pay back to the proud the measure of their deeds that they deserve.
How long will the wicked boast, Lord, and exult with pompous nerve?

All their words are full of boasting, and they pour out arrogance.
Lord, they crush, oppress Your people, those of Your inheritance.
They slay foreigner and widow, kill the fatherless like weeds.
They say, “For the Lord does not see; Jacob’s God—He pays no heed.”

O you senseless, foolish people, when will you take heed, be wise?
Won’t He hear who made the ear, and won’t He see who made the eyes?
He who acts will strike the nations; He who teaches, won’t He know?
The Lord knows the thoughts of man and how they ever futile grow.

Bless-ed is the one You train, Lord, who You teach from Your own law;
You’ll grant him relief from trouble, till in pits the wicked fall.
The Lord won’t reject His people, nor inheritance forget;
Righteous judgment will return and upright hearts will follow it.

Who will rise up ’gainst the wicked? Who will take a stand for me?
Lest the Lord had been my helper, I would dwell in death’s dark sea.
When I said, “My foot is slipping”—Your love, Lord, supported me.
When my soul was anxious in me, You brought solace, joy to me.

Can corrupt thrones be Your partner, who use laws for misery?
They conspire against the righteous, put to death those not guilty.
But the Lord has been my fortress, and my rock in whom I trust;
He’ll repay them for their evil; the Lord will turn them to dust.

title: Psalm 95
lyrics:
Come, let us sing unto the Lord—with joy now let us sing,
And shout to God the Rock of our salvation—songs now bring!
O let us come before Him now with thanksgiving and song,
And in His presence shout with joy, extol Him with a psalm.

For God the Lord is a great God, great King above all gods.
In His hands are the depths of earth, the mountains high and broad.
The sea is His—He is the one who made it by His hand,
And by His hand He also formed all of the earth’s dry land.

Come, let us worship and bow down, before our Maker kneel;
For He’s our God, and we are His, the people of His field.
We are the people in His care, the sheep within His fold;
The people of His pasture whom His loving hand does hold.

Today if you would hear His voice, then harden not your hearts,
As you did when at Meribah your journey had its start.
As in the days of wilderness, at Massah when hungry,
Your fathers, though they’d seen My works, they tried and tested Me.

For forty years My anger with that generation stayed;
I said, “Their hearts go oft astray, and they don’t know My ways.”
So in My anger I declared an oath they’d not be bless’d,
“They surely will not enter in, or ever know My rest.”

title: Psalm 96
lyrics:
O sing to the Lord, a new song now sing.
O sing to the Lord, all earth Your praise bring.
O sing to the Lord and give praise to His name,
And day after day His salvation proclaim.

Among nations all His glory declare,
His marvelous deeds to folk everywhere.
For great is the Lord and most worthy of praise;
He is to be feared above all gods always.

For all of the gods of nations are vain,
The Lord made the heav’ns, and o’er them does reign.
Before Him are splendor and great majesty,
Strength, glory are there in His sanc-tu-ar-y.

Ascribe to the Lord, O fam’lies of earth,
Ascribe to the Lord strength, glory, and worth.
Ascribe to the Lord glory due to His name;
Bring off’rings and come to His courts; praise proclaim.

O worship the Lord in splendor of all
His holiness; come and tremble in awe.
Say unto the nations, “The Lord alone reigns!”
The world is established; it firmly remains.

He will judge the peoples with equity,
Let heavens rejoice; let earth joyful be.
Let seas all resound and all that is in them;
Let fields all be joyous, with all things in them.

Then all of the trees will sing forth with joy.
They’ll sing to the Lord; all praise they’ll employ,
Because He is coming, the earth’s judge to be—
He’ll judge earth, all peoples, with true equity.

title: Psalm 97
lyrics:
The Lord reigns, let earth be glad, and let the distant shores rejoice.
Clouds and darkness do surround him; just and righteous is His voice.
Righteousness and justice are the sure foundation of His throne.
Fire goes forth, consumes the wicked; all His foes are overthrown.

The world’s lit up by His lightning; trem-bling seizes all the earth.
Mountains melt like wax before the Lord, who’s Lord of all the earth.
Heav’ns proclaim His righteousness; all peoples do His glory see.
All are shamed who worship idols; worship Him, you gods, humbly!

Zion hears in joyful gladness; towns of Judah all are glad,
Because of Your righteous judgments, O Lord, which have made us glad.
For You are exalted far above all gods that have no worth,
And You are the Lord Most High both here and over all the earth.

Those who love the Lord hate evil, for He guards the lives of those
who are faithful, and delivers them from triumph of their foes.
Light is shed upon the righteous; joy on those upright in heart.
Take joy in the Lord, you righteous; praise unto His name impart.

title: Psalm 98
lyrics:
Sing to the Lord a joyful song,
For He has done great things;
His right hand and His holy arm
salvation to us bring.

The Lord’s salvation is made known,
The nations see it well.
He has recalled His faithfulness,
His love to Israel.

The ends of all the earth have seen
salvation of our God;
Shout to the Lord with joy, all earth,
Burst into joyful song!

Make music to the Lord with harp,
With singing make reply;
With trumpets, horn, and shouts of joy
before the Lord on high.

Let oceans roar and all therein,
All peoples of the earth;
Let rivers clap their hands for joy,
And mountains sing His worth.

For God the Lord is coming soon
to judge the world He made;
He’ll judge the world with equity,
and righteousness displayed.

title: Psalm 99
lyrics:
The Lord God reigns—let nations shake
and tremble before Him;
Let all earth shake—He sits enthroned
between the cherubim.

The Lord is great in Zion, and
all nations He does own.
Let nations praise Your awesome name;
He’s holy—He alone.

The King is mighty, loving right,
And founding equity.
In Jacob, You have done what’s just
and right impeccably.

Exalt the Lord, our mighty God,
and worship at His throne.
Come worship at His footstool, for
He’s holy—He alone.

Aaron and Moses were His priests,
And Samu’l called aloud;
They called the Lord—He answered them,
Spoke to them from the cloud.

They kept His statutes and decrees.
O Lord, You gave them heed—
Were a forgiving God to them,
Yet punished their misdeeds.

Exalt the Lord, the Lord our God
and worship at His throne.
Come worship at His holy hill;
He’s holy—He alone.

title: Psalm 100
lyrics:
Shout out with joy unto the Lord;
Let all the earth now sing!
Come worship; serve with gladness and
your songs before Him bring.

Know that the Lord Himself is God,
He made us—not ourselves.
We are His people and His sheep,
His pasture’s where we dwell.

Enter His gates with thanksgiving;
Into His courts with praise.
Give thanks to Him and bless His name,
His praises sing always.

The Lord is good; His steadfast love
endures forevermore.
His faithfulness from age to age
continues ever sure.

title: Psalm 100
lyrics:
All people that on earth do dwell,
Sing to the Lord with cheerful voice.
Him serve with mirth; His praise forth tell;
Come ye before Him and rejoice.

Know that the Lord is God indeed;
Without our aid, He did us make.
We are His flock; He doth us feed,
And for His sheep He doth us take.

O enter then His gates with praise;
Approach with joy His courts unto.
Praise, laud, and bless His name always,
For it is seemly so to do.

For why? The Lord our God is good;
His mercy is forever sure.
His truth at all times firmly stood,
And shall from age to age endure.

title: Psalm 101
Psalm 102
lyrics:
O hear my prayer, Lord, let my cry for help and mercy come to You;
When I am faint and in distress, don’t hide Your face—keep me in view.
O hear me when I call to You, and answer me—let Your ear turn.
For my days are like smoke consumed, my bones like glowing embers burn.

My heart is withered like the grass, and I forget to eat my food.
Because of groaning, I’m reduced to skin and bones, my life’s consumed.
I’m like a desert owl that sits among the ruins, stark, aloof.
I lie awake; I’m like a bird—a bird alone upon the roof.

Throughout the day my foes taunt me; my name used as a curse appears;
For I eat ashes as my food, and mingle drink with anguished tears.
Because of Your great wrath on me, You take me up, cast me aside.
My days are like the evening shade; I’m like the withered grass that died.

But You, O Lord, do sit enthroned, forever Your renown shall be;”
You will arise, compassion show to Zion as she waits on Thee.
Her time for favor now has come; the time appointed has drawn near.
Your servants pity her great plight; her stones to them are very dear.

All nations and all kings of earth will fear the Lord’s name and revere.
The Lord will rebuild Zion’s place, and in His glory will appear.
He will respond to all the prayers of needy ones who bring their plea.
So write this for the yet unborn, that they may praise the Lord indeed:

“The Lord looked down and viewed the earth; from His Most Holy Place on high;
To hear the pris’ners’ groaning plea, and free the ones condemned to die.”
In Zion and Jerusalem the Lord’s name will be heard, adored;
When peoples and the kingdoms come assemble there to praise the Lord.

He broke my strength in prime of life, and He cut short my length of days.
I said, “Don’t take away my life, God, in the midst of all my days.”
Your years throughout all ages last; in the beginning, God, You laid
the earth’s foundations firm and fast; Your mighty hands the heavens made.

They’ll perish, but You will remain; You shall forevermore endure.
Like garments they will all be changed; they’ll be discarded, worn no more.
But You remain the same and live; Your endless years are ever true.
Your servants, their descendants, too, will be established before You.

title: Psalm 103
lyrics:
Bless the Lord, my soul, let all that is within me bless His name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, forget not all His mercies to proclaim.
He forgives all your transgressions; He heals all disease you face.
He redeems your life forever from the pit with love and grace.

He with good does satisfy you; renews youth like eagle’s flight
He works righteousness and justice for those in oppression’s plight.
He made known His ways to Moses, deeds to Isr’el from above.
The Lord’s gracious with compassion, slow to anger, rich in love.

He will not accuse forever, nor keep anger in reserve;
He does not repay us as our sins and wickedness deserve.
High as heav’ns above the earth, so great His love for all who fear;
Far as east is from the west, He’s cast our sin and drawn us near.

Like a Father has compassion, the Lord pities those who trust;
He knows how we’re formed in frailty, and remembers we are dust.
All our days are like the grass, and like the flower of the field—
When the wind blows, soon it passes—gone its place, no fruit to yield.

His love is with those who fear Him, and His justice will endure,
With all those who keep His cov’nant and obey His statutes sure.
The Lord set His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules o’er all.
Bless the Lord, all you His angels; who obey His ev’ry call.

Bless the Lord, all heav’n-ly hosts who dwell with Him in glory still—
You, His servants, who obey His ev’ry word and do His will.
Bless the Lord, all of His works, from everywhere in His domain.
Bless the Lord, my soul—let nothing but His praise in you remain.

title: Psalm 104
lyrics:
O bless the Lord, my soul; O Lord God, You’re very great!
You’re clothed with majesty, and resplendent is Your state.
He wraps Himself in light, like a garment clothed in rays;
He stretches out the heavens—a canopy of praise.

He builds His heav’nly dwelling on waters in the sky;
He makes the clouds His chariot, on wings of wind He rides.
He makes the winds His servants, with fire His presence proves.
He sets earth on foundations that never can be moved.

You covered earth with water—a garment of the deep;
The waters stood above all the mountain peaks so steep.
But then at Your rebuke, all the waters fled from sight;
At the sound of Your thunder, the waters took to flight.

They flowed over the mountains, went into valleys deep;
You set for them a bound’ry—a bound’ry they must keep.
He makes springs flow ’midst mountains, into ravines they burst;
The creatures all have water; the donkeys quench their thirst.

The birds nest by the waters; they sing among the trees;
And from His heav’nly dwelling, He waters earth with ease.
He makes grass grow for cattle, and plants for man’s good toil;
Gives bread and wine for gladness; makes our face shine with oil.

The Lord’s trees are well watered, the cedars He did plant;
The birds make nests; the stork has a home the pine trees grant.
The goats live in the mountains; the badgers’ needs are met.
The moon marks off the seasons; the sun knows when to set.

You bring the dark at nighttime; the beasts roam forth abroad.
The lions roar for prey, and they seek their food from God.
With rising sun, they go back and lie down in their dens.
Then man goes to his labor, and works till the day ends.

How many are Your works, Lord, in wisdom You made all!
The earth and sea are filled with Your creatures, great and small.
The ships go to and fro; the leviathan live there.
These all look unto You for their food You give with care.

When You open Your hand, and give food to all You’ve made,
They eat it, satisfied with the good that You’ve displayed.
But when You hide Your face, they with fear are terrified;
When You take back their breath, they return to dust and die.

When You send forth Your Spirit, they are created new;
Your Spirit does with power the face of earth renew.
So may the glory of the Lord God endure always,
And may the Lord rejoice in His works that give Him praise.

He looks at earth—it trembles; at His touch, mountains smoke.
I’ll praise the Lord forever; His praise I will invoke.
I’ll sing praise to my God for as long as I may live.
O may my meditation be pleasing which I give.

May my thoughts always please Him, as I joy in the Lord.
But may the sinners perish, and wicked be no more.
O praise the Lord, my soul, and rejoice in Him always;
O bless the Lord, my soul, and forever give Him praise.

title: Psalm 105
lyrics:
Give thanks unto the Lord and call on His name everyone!
Make known among the nations all the wondrous things He’s done.
Sing unto Him, sing praise to Him—tell of His wondrous deeds.
Rejoice and glory in His name, all those who the Lord seek.

Look to the Lord and to His strength, and seek His face always;
Remember wonders He has done for which we give Him praise.
The miracles which His hand wrought and judgments He decreed;
O Abraham’s and Jacob’s seed, His chosen ones indeed.

He is the Lord our God—in all the earth His judgments stand;
And He recalls His cov-e-nant, the words of His command.
For generations vast, He keeps the cov-e-nant He made,
With Abraham and Isaac, too, the promise He conveyed.

To Jacob, also, He confirmed the oath as His decree;
To Is-ra-el the cov-e-nant made everlastingly:
“To you I’ll give the promised land of Canaan where you’ll live;
Your portion and inheritance I will most surely give.”

When they were few in number and were strangers still unknown,
They wandered from one nation to another not their own.
He let no one oppress them, for He told kings for their sake:
“Do not touch My anointed ones, no harm to prophets make.”

He called down famine on the land, destroyed their food supply;
Sent Joseph on before them, sold to slav’ry with a lie.
They bruised his feet with shackles, put his neck in irons, too;
Till what he’d said all came to pass; the Lord’s word proved him true.

The king sent and released him then, the ruler set him free;
He made him master of his house, a ruler then was he.
He taught the princes as he pleased, instruction he did give;
Then Isr’el entered Egypt, and in Ham did Jacob live.

The Lord blessed all His people—they grew more than all their foes,
Whose hearts He turned to hate His flock; His people they opposed.
Then He sent Moses—Aaron too—His servants whom He chose;
And they performed great miracles in Ham’s land, full of foes.

He sent great darkness, for they had rebelled against His word.
He turned their water into blood, their fish died by His word.
Their homes were overrun with frogs—all bedrooms in the land.
He spoke, and there came swarms of flies and gnats throughout the land.

He turned their rain to driving hail with lightning all around;
He struck their vines and fig trees, too; no untouched tree was found.
He spoke and locusts came in droves, grasshoppers everywhere;
They ate up every plant for food; no produce was left there.

Then He struck down all firstborn ones, the first sons of their womb.
He brought out Isr’el, all their tribes, with gold and silver too.
Egypt was happy when they left, they dreaded Isr’el’s might.
He gave a cloud for cov’ring, and a fire for light at night.

They asked and He brought quail to them—from heaven gave them bread;
He opened rocks and water gushed like rivers’ fountainhead.
For He remembered promises He made to Abraham;
He brought His people out with joy—His chosen ones from Ham.

He gave them lands of nations that they gained by His defense—
What others toiled for, they received as their inheritance,
That they would keep His covenant, His precepts, and His laws.
O praise the Lord, remember well; O praise Him, peoples all!

title: Psalm 106
lyrics:
Praise to the Lord, Give thanks, for He is good;
His love endures forever and always.
Who can proclaim His mighty acts and deeds,
Or fully tell of all the Lord’s great praise?

Bless’d are the ones who justice do maintain;
Who constantly do right with courage brave.
Remember me, O Lord, when You show grace;
Come to my aid when You Your people save.

Then I’ll, like them, enjoy prosperity,
And share with all Your people joyfully.
I’ll join with them, Your own inheritance,
And give You praise with them unendingly.

We have all sinned, just as our fathers did;
We have done wrong and acted wickedly.
Like them in Egypt, when they spurned Your deeds,
Forgot Your love, rebelled by the Red Sea.

Yet He did save them for His own name’s sake,
To make His mighty power known indeed.
He turned the Sea back, dried it up fully;
As through a desert, He then did them lead.

He saved them from the hand of all their foes,
And He redeemed them from their enemy.
The waters drowned their foes—not one survived;
Then they sang praise, and His truth did believe.

But soon they did forget what He had done;
They did not heed His counsel or His rest.
For in the desert, they gave in to greed;
And in the wasteland, put God to the test.

So what they asked for, He did give to them;
But sent on them unbearable disease.
Then in the camp, their jealousy did grow;
Envy for Aaron, Moses, did them seize.

Earth opened up, and swallowed them alive—
Dathan, A-bi-ram, and their company.
Fire blazed among all of their followers,
And flame consumed the wicked thoroughly.

They made a calf at Horeb’s mountain plain;
Worshipped an idol they from metal cast;
Exchanged their Glory for an idol vain—
The image of a bull that feeds on grass.

Thus, they forgot the God who did them save—
Who brought them out from Egypt pow’rfully,
Who did great miracles in land of Ham,
And awesome deeds along the great Red Sea.

He said He would destroy them in His wrath,
Had not His servant Moses intervened—
Stood in the breach and prayed on their behalf,
And from destruction all the people gleaned.

Then they despised the pleasant promised land,
And disbelieved the promise of His word.
They grumbled in their tents against His hand,
And willfully did not obey the Lord.

And so He swore with His uplifted hand;
He’d make them fall within the desert land,
Make their descendants among nations fall,
And scatter them throughout the foreign lands.

They yoked themselves to Ba-al of Peor,
Ate sacrifices offered to vain gods,
Provoked the Lord to anger by their deeds;
A plague broke out among them all abroad.

But Phinehas stood up and intervened;
The plague was stopped when he did intercede.
This was to him as righteousness applied,
For generations who would tell this deed.

Then by the water’s flow at Meribah,
God’s anger came on Moses and on them.
For they rebelled against His Spirit there,
And Moses spoke rash words due to their sin.

Then they refused the nations to destroy,
As God the Lord had so commanded them.
Instead, they mingled with the peoples there,
And followed all their customs in great sin.

They worshipped idols, which became a snare;
To demons, sacrificed their children there.
Innocent blood of daughters and of sons,
They shed to Canaan’s idols without care.

Thus, they defiled themselves by what they did;
They were like prostitutes with arrogance.
The Lord was angry with His chosen ones,
And He abhorred His own inheritance.

He gave them over to the nations ’round;
Their foes ruled over them like a strong tow’r.
Their enemies oppressed them brutally,
And they subjected them to their cruel pow’r.

Many times He delivered them and saved;
But they repeatedly rejected Him.
Bent on rebellion, they did waste away—
Wasted away because of all their sin.

But He saw their distress and heard their cry,
And for their sake, recalled His covenant.
In His great love He turned and did relent,
And in their captors’ eyes, He pity sent.

Save us, O Lord our God, from all our sins;
Gather us from the nations and their ways.
Then we will give thanks to Your holy name,
And we will find our glory in Your praise.

Bless’d be the Lord, the God of Is-ra-el,
From everlasting and forevermore.
Let all the people say, “Amen, Amen!”
Praise to our God—all people, praise the Lord!

title: Psalm 107
lyrics:
O give thanks unto the Lord, for He’s good; His love endures.
Let the Lord’s redeemed say this—those whose lives He has procured
from the hand of all their foes, gathered in from every land;
East and west, from south and north—those He gathered by His hand.

Some in desert wastelands strayed, to a city—found no way;
Filled with hunger and with thirst, till their life did ebb away.
Then they cried out to the Lord, in their trouble and distress;
He led them by a straight way, to a city, safe and bless’d.

Let them give thanks to the Lord, for His steadfast, cov’nant love,
And His wondrous deeds for them, sent unfailing from above.
For the thirsty, He does fill—all their thirst He satisfies;
And the hungry, He feeds still, with good things His hand provides.

Some in darkness and in gloom sat as pri-son-ers in chains,
For they had rebelled ’gainst God, and His counsel did disdain.
Bitter labor God did send; when they stumbled, none would bless.
They cried to the Lord in grief; He saved them from their distress.

Out from darkness and deep gloom, God brought them and broke their chains.
Let them give thanks to the Lord, for His wondrous deeds remain;
Let them praise His steadfast love, which unendingly is ours;
For He breaks down gates of bronze, and cuts through the i-ron bars.

Some were fools with rebel ways; for their sins, in woe were left;
They abhorred all kinds of food; and drew near the gates of death.
Then they cried out to the Lord, in their trouble and distress;
He sent forth His word and healed, rescued them in faithfulness.

Let them give thanks to the Lord, for His steadfast, cov’nant love,
And His wondrous deeds for them, sent unfailing from above.
Let them sacrifice with praise, and with thanks their off’rings make,
Tell of all His works always, sing with joy for His name’s sake.

Others sailed the sea in ships, merchants on the waters’ might.
There they saw the Lord’s great works, wondrous deeds in the deep’s sight.
For He spoke and stirred the waves, tempests lifted high the sea—
Up to heavens, down to depths—peril made their courage flee.

Then they staggered, like drunk men, truly at their own wits’ end;
And they cried out to the Lord in their trouble once again.
Then He brought them from distress; stilled the storm and hushed the waves.
They were glad when all was calm; He had guided them and saved.

Let them give thanks to the Lord, for His steadfast, cov’nant love,
And His wondrous deeds for them, sent unfailing from above.
Let them all exalt His name, as the people gather round;
Council of the elders, too—let their praises all abound.

He turned rivers into sand, springs into a desert land;
Fruitful ground into a waste, due to wicked in the land.
He turned deserts into pools, parched dry ground to flowing springs;
There a city they did found; there the hungry He did bring.

They sowed fields and planted vines, yielding fruitful harvest there.
He bless’d them and they increased, their herds grew without compare.
Then with deep calamity, they were humbled and decreased;
He who has contempt for pride made them wander in stark waste.

But He lifted needy ones out of their affliction’s way;
He increased their fam-i-lies, and their cattle day by day.
Those upright rejoice and see, but the wicked have no word.
Let the wise heed all these things; see the great love of the Lord.

title: Psalm 108
Psalm 109
lyrics:
O God, the One I ever praise, O do not silent be,
For wicked and deceitful men do mock and slander me.
They speak with lies against me and with words of hate surround,
And they attack me without cause—no hope for me is found.

My friendship they return with their accusing everywhere,
But I will not be like them, for I am a man of prayer.
They repay me with wickedness, with evil for my good,
And hatred for the friendship I would offer if I could.

Appoint a wicked man to stand against him to oppose;
Let an accuser stand at his right hand with all his foes.
When he’s tried, let him guilty be; his very prayers condemn;
His days be few; another take his leadership from him.

May his wife soon a widow be; his children fatherless;
May they be wand’ring beggars with no home or kind redress.
May creditors seize all he has; his work to strangers’ greed;
May none their kindness give to him, nor take care of his seed.

May his descendants be cut off—their names forgotten be.
May God recall his fathers’ sins; his mother’s also see.
May all their sins remain before the Lord since days of birth;
May He cut off the mem-or-y of them from all the earth.

For he of kindness never thought, but hounded unto death
the brokenhearted and the poor; he took their very breath.
He loved to curse—so cursing therefore also came on him;
He found no joy in blessing, therefore blessing’s far from him.

He clothed himself with cursing as a garment that he wore;
It entered to his inward parts like water and like oil.
So it will be to him just like a cloak wrapped ’round about,
And like a belt that constantly girds all his life throughout.

May this be the Lord’s payment to accusing enemies;
To those who with great malice speak their evil against me.
But You, O sovereign Lord, deal well with me for Your name’s sake;
In goodness of Your love, save me, and don’t my life forsake.

For I am poor and needy, and my heart’s pierced in my soul.
I fade away like evening shade; cast off like locusts whole.
My knees give way from fasting, and my frame is gaunt and thin.
When they see me, they wag their heads; I’m just a scorn to them.

Help me, O Lord, and save me in accordance with Your love;
Let them know that it’s from Your hand—You’ve done it from above.
For they may curse, but You will bless, though they curse with their voice;
When they attack, they’ll be shamed but Your servant will rejoice.

Accusers will be clothed with shame, like a robe of disgrace.
With my mouth I’ll extol the Lord, bring praise before His face.
For He stands at the right hand of the needy one ’gainst them;
To save his life from those who would judge him and would condemn.

title: Psalm 110
lyrics:
The Lord says to my Lord: “Come sit at my right hand until
I make your enemies a stool whereon your feet may dwell.”

The Lord will stretch your scepter to extend from Zion’s hill;
You’ll rule amidst your enemies; you will rule ever still.

Your troops will be a willing force on this your battle day;
The youth will come from early dawn in majesty arrayed.

The Lord has sworn His promise and He will not change His mind:
“You are a priest forever in Melchizedek’s own line.”

The Lord is at Your right hand – He is at Your hand and path;
And He will crush rebellious kings on the day of His wrath.

He’ll judge the nations, heaping up the bodies of the dead,
And crushing rulers of the earth who see His day in dread.

He will drink from the brook beside the way His feet do tread;
Therefore, when all is in its place, He will lift up His head.

title: Psalm 111
lyrics:
All praise I’ll give with all my heart,
Bring thanks to God and sing.
Come, gather all you upright ones,
Delight—the Lord is King!

Enjoy the great works of the Lord;
Fail not to see, adore.
Great and majestic are His deeds;
His righteousness endures.

In all my mem’ry He has placed
Just acts and wondrous deeds.
Know that the Lord’s compassionate;
Love and kind grace is He.

Mercy He gives to those who fear,
No food they lack or need.
O He remembers covenant,
Provides eternally.

Quickly He shows His mighty power;
Rewards with gifts of land.
Shows us His just and faithful works;
Trustworthy, His law stands.

Upright and steadfast are His ways;
Vibrant in faithfulness.
Well has He saved His cov’nant ones—
eXtol His holiness!

You will find wisdom when you seek
the fear of God the Lord.
Zealously follow His commands—
praise to Him evermore!

title: Psalm 112
lyrics:
All praise to the Lord Almighty;
Bless’d are those who fear the Lord
Come and revel in His statutes;
Delight in His righteous Word!

Every child of God Almighty,
Filled with blessing and set free;
Generations of the upright,
His descendants bless’d shall be.

In his house will be true riches;
Justice, righteousness endure.
Kindled light into the darkness,
Love and mercy there are sure.

Mighty is the one who’s gen’rous,
Never failing to be just;
Openhearted, never shaken,
Praise is his e’en from the dust!

Quiet trust despite bad tidings,
Resolute trust in the Lord.
Steadfast is his fearless stature,
Triumph o’er his foes is sure.

Upright, just, he gives so freely,
Visiting the poor with food;
With his righteousness enduring,
eXalted in honor, good!

Yes, the wicked man will see, and
in his anger, gnash his teeth.
Zeal for right will be exalted
when his ending is complete!

title: Psalm 113
lyrics:
Praise the Lord, sing hallelujah! Praise, O servants of the Lord;
Bless-ed be the Lord’s name ever—praise Him now and evermore.
From the rising of the sun to where it sets at end of day,
The Lord’s name is to be praised in ev’ry place the sun has sway.

For the Lord is high above the nations of earth everywhere,
And His glory is exalted o’er the heav’ns, none can compare.
Who is like the Lord our God—the One who sits enthroned on high?
He who stoops to look upon all on the earth from heaven high.

He does raise the poor from dust; lifts needy ones from the ash heap;
He seats them with princes, and with princes He their lives will keep.
He will give the barren woman joy in children all her days;
In a home she will abide—O to the Lord be joyful praise!

title: Psalm 114
lyrics:
When Isr’el out of Egypt came, from those they dwelt among;
When Jacob’s house went out from those that were of foreign tongue;

Then Judah did God’s house become, and Isr’el His domain.
The sea did look and fled away; the Jordan did the same.

The mountains, they did skip like rams; the hills, like little lambs.
Why was it, sea, that you did flee? Why turn back, Jordan’s dam?

Why, mountains, did you skip like rams? You hills, like lambs adored?
O tremble, earth, for you are in the presence of the Lord!

The God of Jacob’s presence, He who from the rock did bring
a pool of water, turned hard rock into a fountain spring.

title: Psalm 115
lyrics:
Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to Your name glory be;
Because of Your lovingkindness, and Your truth shown faithfully.
Why do nations ask in wonder, “Where’s their God? We don’t see Him.”
Our God is in heaven, and He does whatever pleases Him.

Their gods are of gold and silver; made by hands of men are they.
They have mouths, but cannot speak; they’ve eyes, but cannot see the day.
They have ears, but cannot hear, and noses but they cannot smell;
They have hands, but cannot feel, and feet that can’t walk—know this well.

They can’t make a sound with their throat, cannot say a word at all;
Those who make them will be like them, unable on God to call.
Everyone who trusts in idols will become like idols vain.
House of Isr’el, trust the Lord; He does your help and shield remain.

House of Aaron, put your trust in God the Lord, your help and shield;
You who fear the Lord, so trust Him—He is all your help and shield.
He remembers and will bless the house of Isr’el, Aaron, too.
He’ll bless those who fear the Lord; the small and great alike, renew.

May the Lord make you increase; both you and all your children, too;
May you be bless’d by the Lord, the Maker of earth, heaven, too.
For the highest heav’ns belong to God the Lord, to Him alone,
But the earth to man is given, to take care of as his own.

It is not the dead who praise Him—those who down to silence go;
It is we who praise the Lord, all those who His great name do know.
We will bless the Lord forever, from this time forevermore;
We, the living ones will praise Him; all who live now praise the Lord!

title: Psalm 116
lyrics:
I love the Lord, because He hears my voice;
He hears the cry for mercy which I give.
Because He turned His ear to answer me,
I’ll call upon Him as long as I live.

The cords of death ensnared, entangled me;
The grave’s dark anguish, sorrow like a sea.
Then I called on the name of God the Lord:
“O Lord, come rescue and deliver me!”

The Lord is gracious, full of righteousness;
Our God has great compassion upon all.
The Lord protects the simplehearted ones;
He saved me, when in great need I did call.

Now be at rest again, once more, my soul;
The Lord has been good to you in all things.
For Lord, You have delivered me from death,
My eyes from tears, my feet from stum-bl-ing.

Thus, I shall walk before the Lord, my God,
In the land of the living, bright as day.
I believed e’en when I said, “I’m distressed.”
“All men are liars,” I said in dismay.

What shall I render, then, unto the Lord,
For all His goodness, and His love to me?
I will lift up the cup of salvation,
And call upon the Lord’s name earnestly.

I will fulfill my vows unto the Lord;
May it be in the presence of His saints.
For precious in the sight of God the Lord
is e’en the death of all His faithful saints.

O Lord, I am Your faithful servant true,
You’ve loosed my chains, the son of Your handmaid.
I’ll sacrifice a thank off’ring to You,
and call upon the Lord’s name unafraid.

I will fulfill my vows unto the Lord
within the presence of His saints abroad;
Within the courts of the house of the Lord,
In your midst, O Jerus’lem. Praise the Lord!

title: Psalm 117
lyrics:
Praise give the Lord, you nations all;
All peoples, praise now bring.
Extol the Lord, you peoples all,
Extol Him—praise and sing!

His lovingkindness does abound;
His love toward us is sure.
The Lord’s great faithfulness endures
Forever—praise the Lord!

title: Psalm 118
Psalm 119
lyrics:
[Aleph]

How bless’d are those who keep their way
as blameless and complete;
Who make the law of God the Lord
the path that guides their feet.

How bless’d are those who do observe
His testimonies sure;
Who seek the Lord with all their heart
and keep their actions pure.

They do no wrong, but walk within
the ways He has ordained;
You gave Your precepts so they’d be
obeyed and not disdained.

Oh, that my ways were steadfastly
aligned with Your decrees!
Then I would not be put to shame
when Your commands I see.

I’ll give You thanks with a right heart
when Your right laws I learn.
I’ll keep Your statutes; O, do not
forsake or from me turn!

[Beth]

How can a youth keep his way pure?
Live as Your word demands!
I’ve sought You wholly; don’t let me
stray from Your pure commands.

Your word I’ve hidden in my heart,
That I won’t sin ’gainst You.
Praise be to You, O Lord my God,
Teach me Your statutes true.

I have recounted with my lips
the laws Your mouth has told.
I have rejoiced in following
Your statutes more than gold.

I’ll meditate upon Your ways,
Your precepts I have heard.
I will delight in Your decrees;
I won’t forget Your word.

[Gimel]

Do good unto Your servant—thus,
I’ll live and keep Your word.
Open my eyes that I may see
great things Your law has stirred.

I am a sojourner on earth;
Don’t hide commands from me.
My soul longs for Your ord’nances,
seeks Your laws constantly.

The arrogant You do rebuke,
Who stray from Your commands.
Take scorn from me, for I observe
Your testimonies grand.

Though rulers sit and slander me,
I treasure Your decrees.
Your statutes are my pure delight,
like coun-se-lors to me.

[Daleth]

My soul clings to the dust—revive
according to Your word.
I’ve told my ways—You answered me;
Teach me decrees I’ve heard.

Make me to know Your precepts’ ways;
I’ll ponder wonders heard.
My soul’s weighed down with grief—give strength,
According to Your word.

Remove from me deceitful ways;
Your law to me is grace.
I chose to walk the way of truth:
Your laws before my face.

I hold fast to Your statutes, Lord;
Let shame not cover me.
I’ll run the way of Your commands;
My heart has been set free!

[He]

Teach me Your statutes’ way, O Lord,
I’ll keep it to the end.
Give understanding of Your law;
It’s ever my heart’s friend.

Make me to walk with pure delight
in Your commandments’ reign;
Incline my heart to Your decrees
and not to selfish gain.

Turn my eyes from all worthless things;
Revive me in Your ways.
Fulfill Your promise, so that You
will be feared with true praise.

Turn back my dreaded shame, disgrace;
Your laws are good and strong.
Revive me in Your righteousness;
For Your precepts I long.

[Vav]

May Your unfailing love, O Lord,
Come to me in Your word.
Then I will answer those who taunt,
For I trust in Your Word.

Don’t take Your word of truth from me;
My hope is in Your laws.
I’ll keep Your law continually,
Forever without pause.

I’ll walk about in liberty,
Your precepts I have sought.
I’ll speak Your statutes before kings
without shame as I ought.

I’ll take delight in Your commands;
I love them endlessly.
I lift my hands to Your commands
and ponder Your decrees.

[Zayin]

Recall Your word, which made me hope
ev’n in the midst of strife.
This is my comfort in distress:
Your promise gives me life.

The arrogant deride and scorn;
Your law I won’t forsake.
Your ordinances, Lord, of old—
In them, I comfort take.

I am indignant ’gainst all those
who won’t Your law obey.
Your statutes are my songs within
my pilgrim’s homeward way.

Lord, I recall Your name at night,
And I will keep Your law.
This is my practice: I obey
Your precepts one and all.

[Heth]

The Lord’s my portion; I have vowed:
Your words I will obey.
With all my heart, I seek Your face;
Your promise, grace conveys.

I searched my ways—turned my steps to
Your testimonies grand;
I hastened, and did not delay
to keep all Your commands.

Though cords of wicked ones snare me,
I’ll not forget Your law.
At midnight I’ll give thanks to You,
Your righteous laws recall.

To all who fear You, I’m a friend,
Those who Your precepts keep.
The earth’s full of Your love, O Lord;
Teach me Your statutes deep.

[Teth]

Do good unto Your servant, Lord,
according to Your Word.
Teach me discernment; I believe
in Your commands I’ve heard.

Before affliction came, I strayed,
but now I keep Your Word.
For You are good, and do what’s good;
Teach me Your statutes, Lord.

The arrogant smear me with lies;
Your precepts hold my heart.
Their hearts are hard, but I delight
in what Your law imparts.

It’s good that I bore suffering;
I learned from Your decrees.
The law from Your mouth is more dear
than gold or silver heaps.

[Yodh]

Your hands made me and fashioned me;
Help me learn Your commands.
Those who fear You see me with joy;
My hope in Your word stands.

Your judgments, Lord, I know are right;
You chasten faithfully.
May Your love comfort me because
Your promise is for me.

May Your compassion bring me life;
Your law is my delight.
May arrogant be shamed for lies;
I’ll learn Your precepts right.

May those who fear You turn to me;
They know Your statutes’ way.
May my heart hold to Your decrees;
That shame with me won’t stay.

[Kaph]

My soul longs for Your salvation;
In Your word hopes fully.
My eyes fail looking for Your word.
“When will You comfort me?”

Though I’m like wineskin in the smoke,
Your laws shine o’er my woes.
How long must I, Your servant, wait?
When will You judge my foes?

The arrogant dig pits for me;
They don’t regard Your laws.
All Your commands are trustworthy;
I’m wronged without a cause.

Help me! They would destroy my life;
I’ve kept Your precepts’ way.
Revive me in Your steadfast love;
Your statutes I’ll obey.

[Lamedh]

Eternal is Your word, O Lord;
In heaven firm it stands.
Your faithfulness lasts for all time;
Like earth formed by Your hands.

Your laws endure until this day,
For You’re served by all things.
Had Your law not been my delight,
I’d die from suffering.

I’ll not forget Your precepts, for
by them my life’s revived.
Preserve me, I am Yours; for by
Your precepts I’ve survived.

The wicked wait to kill me, but
Your statutes I’ll hold fast.
To all perfection, there’s an end,
But Your commands are vast.

[Mem]

O, how I love Your law, it is
my meditation sure.
I’m wiser than my enemies
from Your commandments, Lord.

I’ve insight more than those who teach;
Your statutes are my way.
I understand more than the old;
Your precepts I obey.

I’ve kept my feet from evil ways,
That I may keep Your word.
I’ve not turned from Your ord’nances;
You’ve taught me, and I’ve heard.

How sweet Your words are to my taste;
Yes, more than honey sweet.
Your precepts understanding give;
I hate all wrong I meet.

[Nun]

Your word’s a lamp unto my feet,
A light unto my path.
I’ve sworn to keep Your righteous laws;
Confirmed them as my path.

I am afflicted—save me, Lord,
According to Your word.
Accept, O Lord, my willing praise;
Teach me Your laws I’ve heard.

My life’s in danger constantly;
I won’t forget Your law.
The wicked laid a snare for me;
Your precepts I’ll recall.

Your statutes are my heritage,
My heart’s joy and my friend.
My heart is set on Your decrees,
Forever, to the end.

[Samekh]

All double-minded ones I hate,
But love Your law I’ve heard.
You are my hiding place and shield;
My hope is in Your word.

Depart from me, all evil ones;
I keep my God’s commands.
Sustain me in Your promises;
My life is in Your hands.

And let me not be put to shame,
Because I hope in Thee.
Uphold me that I may be saved,
And cherish Your decrees.

You cast away the wand’ring ones
who from Your statutes stray.
For their deceitfulness is vain,
And useless is their way.

You discard wicked ones like dross,
Therefore, I love Your law.
My flesh trembles for fear of You,
Your judgments create awe.

[Ayin]

I’ve done what’s just and right, don’t leave
me to oppressors’ sway.
Ensure Your servant’s life, let not
the proud ones have their way.

My eyes for Your salvation long,
Your righteous word to view.
Deal with Your servant in Your love;
Teach me Your statutes true.

I am Your servant; give insight
to know Your statutes all.
It’s time for You to act, O Lord;
they’ve broken all Your law.

Because I love all Your commands,
they make pure gold seem loss;
Because I hold Your precepts right,
I hate each way that’s false.

[Pe]

Your testimonies wondrous are;
My soul loves to obey.
Your words, unfolding, give great light;
The simple grasp their way.

I open wide my mouth and pant,
And long for Your commands.
Turn to me, and have mercy on
those who in Your name stand.

Direct my footsteps in Your word;
let sin not rule o’er me.
Redeem me from oppression, that
I may Your precepts keep.

Make Your face on Your servant shine,
And teach me Your decrees.
My eyes flow streams of tears because
Your law they do not keep.

[Tsadhe]

You only, Lord, are righteous, and
Your judgments all are right.
Your testimonies faithful are
in righteousness and light.

Zeal has consumed me for Your words,
Ignored by ev’ry foe.
Your promises are tested pure;
Your servant loves them so.

Though I’m despised, I don’t forget
Your precepts giv’n to me.
Your righteousness is for all time;
Your law is true indeed.

Though great distress has come on me,
I joy in Your commands.
Your statutes, righteous evermore,
give wisdom, so I stand.

[Qoph]

My heart cries out: O answer, Lord!
Your statutes I’ll obey.
I cry to You: Save me! I’ll keep
Your testimonies’ way.

Before dawn I cry out for help,
I put hope in Your word.
My eyes stay open through the night,
To contemplate Your word.

In lovingkindness, hear my voice,
revive my life, O Lord;
According to Your ord’nances,
preserve my life, O Lord.

All those who follow wickedness
are always drawing near;
But they are far away from You,
And from Your law so dear.

Yet You are near me, O my Lord,
And Your commands are true.
Of old, I’ve known Your statutes are
established firm by You.

[Resh]

Look on my suff’ring—rescue me!
Your law I don’t forget.
Defend my cause, redeem my life;
Your Word revives me yet.

Salvation’s far from wicked ones;
They don’t seek Your decrees.
Great are Your mercies, Lord, revive
me as Your law grants me.

The foes who persecute are great;
Still, I Your statutes keep.
I loathe the faithless, treach’rous ones—
Your word they will not keep.

See how I love Your precepts, Lord;
Revive me in Your love.
Your word is truth; Your righteous laws
forever stand above.

SIN/SHIN
The rulers hate me without cause;
I hold Your word in awe.
I find joy in Your promises,
Like treasure is Your law.

I hate false ways—despise them all—
But how I love Your law!
I praise You seven times each day,
For all Your righteous laws.

Great peace have those who love Your law;
When stumbling comes, they stand.
I hope in Your salvation, Lord,
And follow Your commands.

Your testimonies I obey,
And love them earnestly.
Your statutes, precepts, I do keep;
My ways are known to Thee.

[Tav]

Let my cry come before You, Lord,
Give insight by Your word.
My supplication comes to You;
Deliver by Your word.

May my lips overflow with praise;
You teach me Your decrees.
May my tongue sing, for Your commands
are righteousness indeed.

May Your hand help me, for I chose
Your precepts, good and right.
I long for Your salvation, Lord;
Your law is my delight.

O may I live to praise You, Lord,
May Your laws help me stand.
I’ve strayed like a lost sheep – seek me!
I’ve not lost Your commands.

title: Psalm 120
lyrics:
I call the Lord in my distress
and He does answer me.
O save me, Lord, from lying lips
and tongues that speak deceit.

What will He do to you, O tongue,
Deceitful as you be?
He’ll punish you with arrows sharp
and coals of the broom tree.

O woe to me that I sojourn
and dwell in Meshech’s land;
I am a pilgrim living where
the tents of Kedar stand.

Too long I’ve lived where peace is scorned
and hated and abhorred;
I am for peace, but when I speak,
they only are for war.

title: Psalm 121
lyrics:
I lift my eyes up to the hills—
Where does my help come from?
My help comes from the Lord, who made
the heav’ns and earth—it comes!

He won’t allow your foot to slip;
His watch o’er you He keeps.
For He who watches Israel—
